prompt: A student wants to add this sentence to the paragraph: "Then he leads us up a dirt path to the rows of apple trees." Where should it be added?
passage: (1) Every fall, our class takes a field trip to Hilltop Farm. (2) When we arrive, the farmer gives each of us a basket. (3) We walk through the orchard and pick as many apples as we can carry. (4) Back at the barn, we wash the apples and press them into cider. (5) At the end of the day, everyone takes home a jar.
why_wrong: places "he" before the farmer has been mentioned
places the walk to the trees after the class is already picking apples
places the walk to the trees after the class is back at the barn
explanation: "He" must refer to the farmer, who first appears in sentence 2, and walking to the trees must come before picking apples in sentence 3. So the sentence belongs after sentence 2.

prompt: A student wants to add this sentence to the paragraph: "Penguins cannot fly, but they are excellent swimmers." Where should it be added?
passage: (1) Their wings work like flippers that push them through the water. (2) Their smooth, rounded bodies help them glide quickly. (3) Some penguins can dive deeper than 500 meters to hunt for fish. (4) After a dive, they often leap out of the water and land on the ice.
why_wrong: places the topic sentence after "Their" has already been used with nothing to refer to
splits the two sentences about body parts
puts the main idea at the very end, after all the details
explanation: Sentence 1 begins with "Their", which has nothing to refer to unless penguins are named first, and the new sentence states the main idea the details support. It belongs before sentence 1.

prompt: A student wants to add this sentence to the paragraph: "The shelter's director thanked her and used the money to buy new blankets for the kennels." Where should it be added?
passage: (1) Lily wanted to raise money for the animal shelter. (2) She decided to sell homemade dog treats at the farmers' market. (3) On Saturday morning, she set up a small table near the entrance. (4) By noon, she had sold every bag and raised eighty dollars. (5) The next week, she gave all of the money to the shelter.
why_wrong: has the director spend money before Lily has sold anything
has the director thank her while she is still setting up
has the director spend the money before Lily gives it to the shelter
explanation: The director can use "the money" only after Lily gives it to the shelter in sentence 5, so the new sentence comes last.

prompt: A student wants to add this sentence to the paragraph: "When lava first pours out, it can be hotter than 1,000 degrees Celsius." Where should it be added?
passage: (1) Volcanoes form where melted rock from deep inside Earth rises to the surface. (2) This melted rock is called magma while it is still underground. (3) Once it pours out onto the surface, it is called lava. (4) As lava cools, it hardens into new rock. (5) Over many eruptions, layers of this rock can build a mountain.
why_wrong: uses the word "lava" before the paragraph explains it
uses "lava" while the paragraph is still describing rock underground
describes how hot fresh lava is after the paragraph has moved on to cooling
explanation: The sentence describes lava just as it erupts, so it belongs after sentence 3, which introduces lava, and before sentence 4, which describes it cooling.

prompt: A student wants to add this sentence to the paragraph: "In October, his coach gave him his first small job, fixing the wiring on the robot's sensors." Where should it be added?
passage: (1) Theo joined the school's robotics team in September. (2) At first, he only watched the older students build and test their robots. (3) By November, he was writing code for the robot's arm. (4) In the spring competition, that arm picked up more blocks than any other team's. (5) Theo now helps new members learn to code.
why_wrong: places his "first" job before the paragraph says he only watched at first
places October after November
places an early job at the end, after he has become a leader
explanation: The paragraph moves in time order: September, "at first", then November. October and a "first small job" fit between watching (sentence 2) and coding in November (sentence 3).

prompt: A student wants to add this sentence to the paragraph: "The magnets pull out steel cans, and jets of air blow light paper off the moving belts." Where should it be added?
passage: (1) Our town's new recycling program began last month. (2) Residents now put paper, plastic and cans together in one blue bin. (3) Trucks collect the bins every Tuesday. (4) At a sorting center, workers separate the materials with machines and magnets. (5) Since the program began, the amount of trash sent to the landfill has dropped by a third.
why_wrong: mentions "the magnets" before any magnets are introduced
describes the sorting before the materials reach the sorting center
puts a detail about sorting after the paragraph has moved to its results
explanation: "The magnets" refers back to the magnets named in sentence 4, and the sentence explains how that sorting works, so it belongs right after sentence 4.

prompt: A student wants to add this sentence to the paragraph: "She uses small scissors so that the stems are cut cleanly instead of torn." Where should it be added?
passage: (1) Hana's grandmother keeps an herb garden on her apartment balcony. (2) She grows basil, mint and rosemary in clay pots. (3) Each morning, she checks the soil with her finger before watering. (4) In the evening, she clips a few leaves to cook with dinner. (5) Hana says the whole apartment smells like the garden.
why_wrong: places the cutting before the paragraph mentions clipping anything
attaches the scissors to watering instead of clipping
places the detail after the paragraph has moved on from the garden work
explanation: The scissors explain how she "clips a few leaves" in sentence 4, so the new sentence belongs right after it.

prompt: A student wants to add this sentence to the paragraph: "Its owner, Mr. Bell, still bakes rye bread from his father's recipe." Where should it be added?
passage: (1) For our history project, Diego and I interviewed Mrs. Rose, who has lived on Cedar Street for sixty years. (2) She told us the street once had a movie theater, a bakery and a shoe repair shop. (3) Only the bakery is still open today. (4) We recorded the interview and turned it into a short podcast. (5) Our teacher played it for the whole class.
why_wrong: places "Its" where it could only mean the street or the project
places "Its" where it could refer to any of three businesses
places "Its" where it would refer to the podcast
explanation: "Its owner" must point to one business that still operates. Sentence 3 names that business (the bakery), so the new sentence goes right after it.

prompt: A student wants to add this sentence to the paragraph: "The reason has to do with how different colors handle sunlight." Where should it be added?
passage: (1) Some cities are painting their rooftops white. (2) Dark roofs absorb sunlight and heat the buildings below them. (3) White roofs reflect much of that sunlight back into the sky. (4) As a result, the buildings stay cooler and need less air conditioning. (5) City planners hope that cooler buildings will also help lower summer temperatures across whole neighborhoods.
why_wrong: announces the explanation after it has already started
announces the explanation after both colors have been explained
announces the reason after the paragraph has given its result
explanation: "The reason" explains why cities paint roofs white (sentence 1) and introduces the explanation of dark and white roofs that begins in sentence 2, so it belongs after sentence 1.

prompt: A student wants to add this sentence to the paragraph: "The town paid for the project with a state grant and money raised by residents." Where should it be added?
passage: (1) The town of Millbrook once depended on a single factory that made wooden furniture. (2) When the factory closed, hundreds of workers lost their jobs. (3) Over the next ten years, the town turned the empty factory into a center for small businesses. (4) Today it holds a pottery studio, a coding school and a bike shop, among others. (5) The building that once employed one company's workers now houses more than thirty businesses.
why_wrong: mentions "the project" before there is any project
mentions "the project" before the town has decided what to do
separates the funding from the project it pays for by placing it after a list of tenants
explanation: "The project" is turning the factory into a business center, introduced in sentence 3, so the sentence about paying for it belongs right after sentence 3.

prompt: Which sentence should be removed because it does not support the main idea of the paragraph?
passage: (1) Our school should make recess fifteen minutes longer. (2) Students who play outside come back to class calmer and ready to focus. (3) A longer recess would also give kids time to finish a whole game of kickball instead of stopping halfway. (4) Kickball is more popular at our school than basketball. (5) Last year, Pine Elementary added ten minutes to recess, and its teachers reported that fewer students were off task in the afternoon. (6) A few extra minutes outside would help everyone.
why_wrong: thinks a claim about focus is off topic because it is about class, not recess
thinks a sentence about kickball cannot support a claim about recess
thinks an example about another school is off topic
explanation: The paragraph argues for a longer recess. Which game is more popular does not support that claim. Sentences 2, 3 and 5 each give a reason or evidence for a longer recess.

prompt: Which sentence should be removed because it does not support the main idea of the paragraph?
passage: (1) Honeybees work together to keep their hive from getting too hot. (2) On warm days, some bees stand at the entrance and fan their wings to move air through the hive. (3) Other bees carry drops of water and spread them on the honeycomb. (4) In winter, the bees cluster tightly together and shiver their muscles to make heat. (5) As the water dries, it cools the air, much like sweat cools a person's skin. (6) Thanks to this teamwork, the hive stays close to the same temperature all summer.
why_wrong: thinks fanning is not teamwork
thinks the comparison to sweat is off topic
thinks the concluding sentence repeats too much
explanation: The paragraph is about how bees keep the hive from getting too hot. Sentence 4 is about warming the hive in winter, a different point, and it also interrupts the water explanation in sentences 3 and 5.

prompt: Which sentence should be removed because it does not support the main idea of the paragraph?

prompt: Which sentence should be removed because it does not support the main idea of the paragraph?

prompt: Which sentence should be removed because it does not support the main idea of the paragraph?

prompt: Which sentence should be removed because it does not support the main idea of the paragraph?
